assumption_ledger.note: The release notes say to audit before removing the shim, but no timeline or owner for shim removal is documented. The audit report (RN-101 deliverable) must include a shim removal decision.

Assuming the canary environment has the dependency-graph fixtures and translator schema available; test_inventory.md only mentions canary coverage exists, not that the environment is configured for this release.
Assuming the kill switch can be toggled without a deploy; no evidence in repo_inventory confirms this operational detail.
assumption_ledger.topic: Rollback procedure for dashboard kill switch

dependency_notes.reason: Fixtures must reflect the audited schema; backfilling before the audit risks encoding stale schema drift.
Dashboard consumes the step-id schema produced by the translator; schema must be stable first.
Dashboard must not ship until dependency-graph fixtures reflect the new schema per dependency_map.md.
Runbook and launch checklist depend on the summary path being proven in canary.

ordered_steps.bounded_deliverable: Schema drift audit report with a decision on shim removal readiness.
ordered_steps.summary: Audit the translator for schema drift before removing the legacy parser shim. The shim currently masks drift in local smoke runs, so this step surfaces the real state of the step-id schema.
ordered_steps.title: Audit translator schema drift

ordered_steps.bounded_deliverable: Updated fixtures that pass tests/plan_contract.py with new step ids.
ordered_steps.summary: Backfill dependency-graph fixtures so the plan contract test catches ordering regressions. Required before the dashboard can ship because the contract test fails when new step ids appear without fixture updates.
ordered_steps.title: Backfill dependency-graph fixtures

ordered_steps.bounded_deliverable: Dashboard summary feature flag gated behind kill switch, canary-validated.
ordered_steps.summary: Enable the translated release-plan dashboard summary behind a kill switch once the schema is stable and fixtures are in place. The dashboard is user-visible and will render whatever order the translator emits.
ordered_steps.title: Enable dashboard summary behind kill switch

ordered_steps.bounded_deliverable: Updated runbook and launch checklist reflecting proven rollout/rollback procedures.
ordered_steps.summary: Update the operator runbook and launch checklist after the summary path is proven in canary. The runbook only stabilizes after rollout and rollback shape are known from the dashboard canary.
ordered_steps.title: Update operator runbook and launch checklist

mitigations: Keep the dashboard behind a kill switch (RN-103) so it can be disabled instantly if bad ordering appears.
Complete the schema audit (RN-101) before any dashboard work to surface hidden drift masked by the shim.
Backfill fixtures (RN-102) and verify plan_contract.py passes before enabling the dashboard in canary.
Limit initial dashboard exposure to canary only, not full rollout.
primary_risk.statement: If the dashboard summary (RN-103) ships before schema audit and fixture backfill are complete, the user-visible release dashboard will render incorrect step ordering, misleading operators during rollout.
